text_blocks.snippet: Common side effects of a COVID-19 booster shot are similar to those experienced after the initial vaccination series and are generally mild and temporary. These include pain or swelling at the injection site, fatigue, headache, muscle pain, chills, fever, and nausea. Some individuals may experience more noticeable side effects, while others may have none at all.
snippet_highlighted_words: pain or swelling at the injection site, fatigue, headache, muscle pain, chills, fever, and nausea

list.snippet: Pain, redness, or swelling at the injection site: This is the most common side effect and can be managed with a cool, damp cloth or ice pack, according to Yale New Haven Health.
Fatigue: Feeling tired or worn out is also frequently reported.
Headache: Headaches are another common side effect.
Muscle pain: Some people experience muscle aches and pains.
Chills: Feeling chilled or shivering can occur.
Fever: A mild fever is possible.
Nausea: Some individuals may experience nausea.
Vomiting: This is less frequent than other side effects.
Diarrhea: Some people may experience diarrhea.
Swollen lymph nodes: Swollen lymph nodes, particularly in the armpit on the side of the injection, can occur.
Side effects typically appear within the first 1-2 days after vaccination and usually resolve within a day or two.
Over-the-counter pain relievers like ibuprofen or acetaminophen can be used to manage side effects, unless otherwise advised by a doctor.

Emergency symptoms: If you experience any severe or concerning symptoms such as trouble breathing, chest pain, confusion, bluish lips or face, or any other sudden and severe symptoms, seek immediate medical attention by calling 911.
Do not take pain relievers preventatively: It is not recommended to take pain relievers before vaccination to prevent side effects, according to the CDC.
